title: Sabaeans
capsule: Saba (Sheba) was an ancient South Arabian kingdom centred in the highlands of what is now Yemen, with its capital at Marib and its power attested from at least the 8th century BCE through the 3rd century CE. The Sabaean mukarribs (priest-kings) built the monumental Marib Dam and controlled the frankincense and myrrh caravan routes linking the Arabian Peninsula to the Mediterranean. Saba competed with and periodically absorbed neighbouring kingdoms such as Qataban and Hadramawt before being eclipsed by the Himyarite Kingdom, which claimed the Sabaean royal title after 275 CE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Sabaean territory around Marib is archaeologically well documented through inscriptions and excavations, but the full extent of political control over caravan routes and client polities remains debated.
